corrections.text: The article states the arXiv paper was 'co-authored by 17 researchers, including Hot Chips presenter Prashant Ranjan of Microsoft and ETH Zurich's Torsten Hoefler.' The 17-author count is correct, but neither cited source identifies a Hot Chips presenter or states any author's institutional affiliation: ServeTheHome's live-blog does not name who presented, and the arXiv abstract page (arxiv.org/abs/2608.24664) lists author names only, with no affiliations. The presenter identification and the 'of Microsoft' / 'ETH Zurich's' affiliations were not sourced from the cited material.

One of the three cited sources, Microsoft's Azure Infrastructure Blog (techcommunity.microsoft.com), returned HTTP 403 (bot-blocked) on both the automated fetch and editorial review's manual re-check, so it could not be independently read. The article's description of the 'two-tier scale-up network' / HammingMesh topology, the Ultra Ethernet Consortium contribution claim, and the '6,143 matrix-multiplication shapes' benchmark methodology rest solely on this unverified source. The accelerator-count figures it underlies (a 48-accelerator rack-scale domain scaling to 6,144 accelerators) are independently consistent with ServeTheHome's separately reported '128 racks with 6000 chips' (48 x 128 = 6,144), and the article already labels the associated 40%-token-generation and 30%-performance-per-dollar figures as Microsoft's own unverified self-reporting.
